requirements.note: Inset-grouped list with Pinned and Notes sections, sorted newest first, with title, a date+preview line and relative dates (time / Yesterday / weekday / short date). Previews truncate early at a word boundary and leave visible empty space.

Filtering by title and body works as you type, and there is a proper 'No Results for …' empty state. But the bottom search field stays behind the keyboard, so you cannot see what you are typing. Matches are not highlighted.
Editing title and body works with no Save button; the edited note moves to the top of Notes and the date updates live to 'Today at …'.
The compose button opens an empty note with the title focused, and Return moves to the body. Leaving an empty note discards it (count stays 90); a note with text is kept (91).
Swipe left gives a native Delete. Pin is only in a long-press context menu; there is no leading swipe to pin. A rightward drag on a row opens the note instead of doing nothing or revealing actions.
'90 Notes' subtitle under the large title, also shown in the inline title; it updates on create and delete.
New note, pin state, deletion and title edits all survived relaunch.

bugs: The search field sits at the bottom and stays under the keyboard when focused, so typed text is hidden (only a faint ghost shows through the keyboard).
Dragging a row to the right opens the note as if it were tapped.
While a row's Delete swipe is open, tapping another row navigates into it instead of just closing the swipe.
In the editor the title is a single-line field that truncates long titles with an ellipsis ('Camera settings for night…'), so you cannot see the whole title while editing it.
tells: When scrolled, the inline nav title and count draw straight over the row text with no proper bar background or scroll-edge treatment, so the text overlaps and is hard to read.
Preview lines truncate several words early ('Ask about podcast…' with lots of room left), which suggests the text is measured by hand rather than by UILabel.
The body placeholder 'Note' in a new note is tiny, widely letter-spaced and in a different-looking font from the body text.
The editor body sits tight against the title with no paragraph spacing.
The 'No Results' title is regular weight, not the bold ContentUnavailableView style.
The editor has no More/share menu, and the toolbar shows only a text 'Done' button while editing.
At the largest text size the editor title truncates to 'Gift ideas fo…'.
At the largest text size the editor body breaks inside a word ('recommendatio/ns').
No leading swipe to pin; pinning is hidden in a long-press menu.
A.scroll: Scrolling is smooth with native deceleration, a rubber-band large title when pulled past the top and no blank rows. The nav title overlapping content while scrolled looks unfinished. Scroll position is kept when returning from a note.

requirements.note: Inset-grouped table with Pinned and Notes sections, sorted newest first, with title, a bold relative/short date and a one-line preview that uses the full width.

Search field in the nav bar moves to the top with a Close button when focused and filters title and body as you type. Matching text is highlighted, body matches show a '…for the landlord.' snippet, and there is a 'No Results for …' empty state with an icon.
Title (multi-line) and body edit in place with no Save button; the note moves to the top of Notes and the edit persists.
The compose button in the bottom toolbar opens a note with the title focused and a yellow Done check. Leaving an empty note discards it (count stays 90); a note with text is kept (91).
Native leading-swipe Pin (orange) and trailing-swipe Delete (red). Tapping elsewhere closes an open swipe. Pinned notes move to the Pinned section.
'90 Notes' in the bottom toolbar like Apple Notes, updated on create and delete.
New note, pin state, deletion and edits all survived relaunch.

tells: The '90 Notes' toolbar count does not grow with Dynamic Type at the largest size.
At the largest text size the editor body/title breaks inside a word ('recommendat/ions', 'recommen-dations' in the list).
The Pinned header spacing shifts a little between launches/returns (header gap grows).
B.scroll: It feels like a native UITableView: smooth drag and fling, proper deceleration and bounce, a nav bar that collapses to an inline title with the search field kept and blurred, no blank or popping rows. Scroll position is kept when returning from a note.

why: B meets every requirement with system-feeling behaviour: leading Pin and trailing Delete swipes, a nav-bar search that stays visible above the keyboard and highlights matches, and an Apple Notes-style toolbar count. A covers most of the spec, but its search field hides behind the keyboard. Its pin action is hidden in a long-press menu, a sideways drag opens notes, and its truncation and nav-bar overlap look unfinished.
